verdict.summary: Using your own Pipedrive OAuth app with your own account is quick, because Composio has no managed Pipedrive OAuth and you register the app yourself in Developer Hub. The hard part is public Marketplace distribution, which Pipedrive approves at its sole discretion and can take up to 21 business days.
verdict.hands_on_effort: About 1-2 hours for a private app connected to your own account (estimate, not sourced). Plan a further several hours to prepare Marketplace review materials (estimate).
verdict.time_to_first_connection: Under an hour once you have a Pipedrive account with Developer Hub access (estimate, not sourced).
verdict.approval_wait: None for private use. Up to 21 business days for public Marketplace review (f17).

gates.name: Own account (developer / sandbox access)
gates.unlocks: Create the OAuth app in Developer Hub, register the Composio callback URL, and connect your own Pipedrive account through Composio.
limits: Developer Agreement says Pipedrive may refuse or terminate sandbox accounts at its discretion (f4).
Sandbox allows at most five Authorized Developer Users (f4).
API access reportedly requires a paid Pipedrive account on any plan (community source, f25). Not confirmed by Pipedrive.
gates.time_to_reach: Minutes, if you already have a paid Pipedrive account or Pipedrive grants a sandbox account.

gates.name: Private / unlisted install (invited users)
gates.unlocks: Install the app for specific companies or users without a Marketplace listing, for non-commercial internal or partner use.
limits: A private app is defined as one used for non-commercial purposes, such as internal use or use by specific clients or partners (f15).
Unlisted apps are described by a community guide as suited to giving some users access (f24). Pipedrive has not confirmed install limits.
Access tokens expire after expires_in (sample value 3599 seconds) and must be refreshed with the refresh_token (f8, f9).
Material changes to a published app need resubmission and 30 days' notice (f22).
gates.time_to_reach: Same day as Gate 1, if the app is used only internally.

gates.name: Public Marketplace listing
gates.unlocks: Any Pipedrive company can find and install the app from the Marketplace.
limits: Approval is at Pipedrive's sole discretion and final (f14).
Approved apps are unlisted by default until you click Publish in Developer Hub (f21).
Rejected apps receive an email with reasons and must be fixed and resubmitted (f21).
Demo video, fully working test accounts and a reachable contact are required (f13, f20).
gates.time_to_reach: Up to 21 business days for public review after submission (f17), plus fixing any rejection reasons and clicking Publish.

steps.title: Confirm you need your own app
steps.detail: Composio lists no managed OAuth for Pipedrive, so you must register your own app and give Composio its client ID and secret. Decide now whether the app is private (internal or specific clients) or public (Marketplace), because that changes the review path later.
gotchas: Composio's default scope list is Composio's choice, not a Pipedrive requirement.

steps.title: Get a Pipedrive account with developer access
steps.detail: Sign up for a Sandbox Account from developers.pipedrive.com, then log in to Pipedrive. Pipedrive may refuse or end sandbox access, and the community view is that API access needs a paid account, so have a paid account as a fallback.
gotchas: The sandbox allows at most five Authorized Developer Users (f4).
Whether a free sandbox is enough to create a public app is not confirmed (see open questions).

steps.title: Open Developer Hub
steps.detail: In Pipedrive, go to Settings, then your company's Developer Hub. Register the app there.

steps.title: Register the OAuth app and set the redirect URI
steps.detail: Create a new app in Developer Hub. In the registration form, enter the callback URL from your Composio auth config. Pipedrive only sends the authorization code to a callback that matches the value you entered here.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: A mismatched callback returns an error at authorization. Copy the value exactly, with no trailing slash added or removed.
Redirect URI rules (HTTPS, localhost, number allowed) are not confirmed by the findings.

steps.title: Copy the client ID and client secret into Composio
steps.detail: Copy the client_id and client_secret that Developer Hub issues for the app. Paste them into the Pipedrive OAuth2 auth config in Composio. Pipedrive's token exchange uses these two values in HTTP Basic auth.
gotchas: An invalid client_id returns HTTP 401 with a message pointing to developers.pipedrive.com. Re-copy the ID if you see this (f3).

steps.title: Set scopes and keep them minimal
steps.detail: Select only the scopes your agent needs in the app's scope settings and in the Composio auth config. The six scopes below are Composio's defaults, not Pipedrive-verified requirements. Each scope you request will be reviewed in the Marketplace demo video.

values.label: Composio default scopes
values.value: contacts:full, leads:full, mail:full, activities:full, products:full, projects:full

gotchas: The consent page explains the scopes you set to the user, so keep the list short (f11).
The full Pipedrive scope list is not verified by the findings.

steps.title: Connect your own account through Composio
steps.detail: Run a test authorization from Composio using your own Pipedrive account. The consent page shows the app name, company and scopes; click Allow and install. Confirm the connection returns a token and the company API domain.
gotchas: The authorization code expires in 5 minutes, so complete the exchange promptly (f10).
The token response includes scope 'base' and a company-specific api_domain (f12).

steps.title: Verify token refresh and the Marketplace OAuth requirement
steps.detail: Confirm the connection refreshes after expires_in (sample 3599 seconds) using the refresh_token at the token endpoint. Also confirm the OAuth flow is still current, since Pipedrive reports v1 endpoints out of support from Aug 1, 2026.
gotchas: Pipedrive's OAuth reference is under the v1 docs path, so check the current docs before you rely on them (f23).

steps.title: Choose the distribution path
steps.detail: If the app is only for your company or named clients, keep it private and install it directly without Marketplace submission. For wider distribution without a public listing, consider an unlisted app, but Pipedrive has not confirmed install caps for it. Public Marketplace listing requires review.
gotchas: Pipedrive's OAuth docs say OAuth is necessary for Marketplace apps and for installs outside the Marketplace (f6).

steps.title: Install for test users and check the limits
steps.detail: Install the app for your test companies or users and confirm the token refresh works for each one. Record any install caps you hit, since the findings do not confirm them.
gotchas: The five-user sandbox limit applies to developer access, not to customer installs (f4).
Pipedrive does not confirm user or install caps for unlisted apps.

steps.title: Draft legal pages and listing documentation
steps.detail: Draft a Terms of Service page and a Privacy Policy webpage, plus listing and documentation text that accurately describes what the app does with each scope. Check that nothing infringes trademarks and that no spam is sent to emails pulled from connected accounts. You must publish the pages on your own domain and keep them current.
gotchas: The Privacy Policy must be on a webpage you maintain, not only in the app.
Pipedrive's legal checklist also covers trademark and copyright and spam rules (f19).

steps.title: Prepare the review pack
steps.detail: Record a demo video that shows how the app uses each permission and scope. Set up fully working, up-to-date test accounts for Pipedrive's reviewers. Name a reachable contact for questions during review.
gotchas: Questions go to marketplace.devs@pipedrive.com (f17).

steps.title: Submit the app for Marketplace review
steps.detail: Submit the app for approval from Developer Hub, with the demo video, test accounts and privacy policy URL. Approval is at Pipedrive's sole discretion, so a rejection is possible even if the pack is complete.
gotchas: Pipedrive's Developer Agreement says approval is final at its discretion (f14).

steps.title: Wait for review
steps.detail: Pipedrive may take up to 21 business days to review a public app. If rejected, you receive an email with the reasons and must fix them before resubmitting.
gotchas: Public reviews may take up to 21 business days (f17).

steps.title: Publish the approved app
steps.detail: After approval the app stays unlisted from the Marketplace until you click Publish in Developer Hub. Any later material change to a published app must be resubmitted, with at least 30 days' written notice to Pipedrive and clients.
gotchas: Material changes and removal need 30 days' prior written notice (f22).

blockers.symptom: No managed Pipedrive OAuth in Composio; the connection cannot be made with Composio's app.
blockers.cause: Composio lists managed_oauth_available as false for Pipedrive.
blockers.fix: Register your own OAuth app in Pipedrive Developer Hub and supply its client ID and secret to Composio.

blockers.cause: Pipedrive may refuse or terminate sandbox accounts at its discretion.
blockers.fix: Use an existing paid Pipedrive account with developer access, or contact Pipedrive through the developer site.

blockers.symptom: Authorization fails with an invalid client error (HTTP 401).
blockers.cause: The client_id is wrong or not issued for this app.
blockers.fix: Re-copy the client ID from Developer Hub and check the redirect URI matches.

blockers.symptom: Marketplace submission rejected or not approved.
blockers.cause: Approval is at Pipedrive's sole discretion and is final. Rejected apps must be fixed and resubmitted.
blockers.fix: Read the rejection email, fix the listed issues, and resubmit. Questions go to marketplace.devs@pipedrive.com.

blockers.symptom: Marketplace review takes longer than expected.
blockers.cause: Public reviews may take up to 21 business days.
blockers.fix: Plan around the 21-business-day window and keep the review contact reachable.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth for Pipedrive. Register your own app in Pipedrive Developer Hub and paste its client ID and secret into the Composio OAUTH2 auth config. Composio's default scopes are its own choice, not a Pipedrive requirement. Internal-only apps can skip Marketplace submission, per the Composio findings.

evidence.claim: Composio's toolkit record lists Pipedrive's OAuth2 authorize and token endpoints under oauth.pipedrive.com, with managed OAuth not available.
evidence.quote: "managed_oauth_available": false

evidence.claim: The Marketplace OAuth guide says the authorization code expires in 5 minutes.
evidence.quote: Note that the `authorization_code` expires in **5 minutes**.

evidence.claim: The consent page shows the app's title, company name and icon, and explains the permission scopes the developer set for the app; the user then clicks Allow and install or Cancel.
evidence.quote: explain the permission scopes that you have set for the app

evidence.claim: The sample token response shows scope value 'base' and an api_domain of the customer's company subdomain, which means the token response returns the company-specific API host.
evidence.quote: "scope": "base"

evidence.claim: Marketplace review asks developers to demonstrate in a demo video how the app uses its permissions and scopes, so scope choices are examined during review.
evidence.quote: Provide our team with a demo video in which you explain the usage of permissions and scopes

evidence.claim: The Developer Agreement requires Marketplace apps to be submitted for Pipedrive approval, and approval is at Pipedrive's sole discretion and final.
evidence.quote: The decision to approve or not approve a Marketplace App at any point is at Pipedrive’s sole discretion and any such decision is final.

evidence.claim: The Developer Agreement defines a Private App as one used for non-commercial purposes, such as internal use or use by specific clients or partners without broader commercial distribution.
evidence.quote: "Private App" means the one or more applications that are developed by Developer and designed to interoperate with the Pipedrive Services for non-commercial use

evidence.claim: Approval requirements in the Developer Agreement include accurate contact information, a current privacy policy on the developer's webpage, and listing and documentation that accurately describe the app.
evidence.quote: provide and maintain an up-to-date privacy policy on their webpage

evidence.claim: Pipedrive's app approval guide says public review may take up to 21 business days, with questions to marketplace.devs@pipedrive.com.
evidence.quote: public app reviews may take up to 21 business days

evidence.claim: Pre-submission steps: request a developer sandbox account, then in Pipedrive go to Settings and the company Developer Hub to register the listing, install and test, and preview it.
evidence.quote: Log into your Pipedrive account and go to Settings > (company name) Developer Hub

evidence.claim: The approval guide's legal checklist requires a Terms of Service page, a Privacy Policy webpage, no trademark or copyright infringement, and no spam sent to emails pulled from connected accounts.
evidence.quote: Your app has a Privacy Policy webpage of a legal document

evidence.claim: Composio's default Pipedrive scopes are contacts, leads, mail, activities, products and projects at full access. These are Composio defaults, not Pipedrive-verified review requirements.
evidence.quote: contacts:full, leads:full, mail:full, activities:full, products:full, projects:full

evidence.claim: For review, the app must supply a demo video, fully working test accounts, and a reachable contact for questions during approval.
evidence.quote: Provide our team with fully functional and up-to-date test accounts

evidence.claim: Rejected apps get an email with the reasons and must fix them before resubmitting; approved apps are unlisted from the Marketplace by default until the developer clicks Publish in Developer Hub.
evidence.quote: The app is unlisted from the Marketplace by default after approval.

evidence.claim: Material changes to a published Marketplace app must be resubmitted for approval, and developers must give at least 30 days' notice before material changes or removal.
evidence.quote: provide at least thirty (30) days’ prior written notice to Pipedrive and all Clients

evidence.claim: The API changelog shows v1 endpoints out of support as of Aug 1, 2026, and Projects API v2 and new webhooks added in May 2026.
evidence.quote: Reminder: Deprecated API v1 endpoints are now out of support

evidence.claim: A community guide says Pipedrive offers unlisted apps for providing an integration to only some users; Pipedrive has not confirmed install limits for these.
evidence.quote: Unlisted apps are suitable if you want to provide a Pipedrive integration to only some users.

evidence.claim: A third-party review says API access requires a paid Pipedrive account on any plan, with a Lite tier at $14 per seat per month including full API access (August 2026 write-up).
evidence.quote: Getting API access requires a paid Pipedrive account on any plan.

evidence.claim: OIDC discovery on pipedrive.com returned 404, so no OpenID Connect discovery document is advertised there; endpoints and scopes must come from Pipedrive's docs.
The authorize endpoint is live: an invalid client_id returns HTTP 401 JSON that points developers to the Pipedrive developer site.
evidence.quote: "error_info":"Please check developers.pipedrive.com"

evidence.claim: The Pipedrive Developer Agreement says developers can request a sandbox account, which Pipedrive may refuse or terminate at its discretion, and the sandbox allows at most five Authorized Developer Users.
evidence.quote: The maximum number of Authorized Developer Users that can access the sandbox is five (5)

evidence.claim: The developer homepage offers sandbox account sign-up and pitches Marketplace reach to over 100,000 companies; it is public and has no login wall.
evidence.quote: Sign up for a Sandbox Account today to begin experimenting and developing in a risk free environment

evidence.claim: Pipedrive's OAuth 2.0 reference says OAuth is required for apps published in the Marketplace, and the authorize step is needed only when installation happens outside the Marketplace.
evidence.quote: Using OAuth 2.0 is necessary for developing apps that are available in the Pipedrive Marketplace.

evidence.claim: Authorization requires a client_id issued at app registration and a redirect_uri that must match the callback URL entered in the registration form.
evidence.quote: The callback URL you provided when you registered your app. Authorization code will be sent to that URL (if it matches with the value you entered in the registration form)

evidence.claim: The token exchange uses HTTP Basic auth built from client_id and client_secret, and the reference's sample response shows expires_in of 3599 seconds and a refresh_token.
evidence.quote: Base 64 encoded string containing the `client_id` and `client_secret` values.

evidence.claim: The access token expires after the period in expires_in and must then be refreshed with the refresh_token via the token endpoint.
evidence.quote: The `access_token` has a lifetime. After a period of time, which was returned to you in `expires_in` JSON property, the `access_token` will be invalid

open_questions: Full Pipedrive scope list and which scopes trigger extra review are unverified. Composio's six defaults are not confirmed as Pipedrive requirements.
Redirect URI rules (HTTPS requirement, number allowed, localhost handling) and PKCE support are not confirmed.
Install caps and user limits for unlisted or private apps are not confirmed by any primary source.
Whether a free sandbox account is enough to create a public app, or whether an org admin or paid plan is needed, is not confirmed.
Whether a direct install link is available for private apps is not confirmed by the findings.
Marketplace listing requirements beyond the approval guide (logo, description, minimum installs, security assessment) are not verified.
